subject.title: fix(scripts): warn when postinstall detects running gateway with stale module imports

question: Should OpenClaw accept npm postinstall loopback probing plus a new opt-out env var as the stale-gateway mitigation surface, or prefer the update/runtime/doctor warning boundary instead?
rationale: The code can be repaired mechanically, but adding a network probe during package installation and a new env suppression surface is a product/operator decision.

options.title: Accept postinstall advisory after repair
options.body: Keep this PR direction if it becomes profile-aware and includes real postinstall warning proof for a listening gateway.

options.title: Prefer update-CLI warning
options.body: Use the overlapping update-flow PR for version-changing updates and leave package-manager postinstall behavior unchanged.

options.title: Require runtime or doctor detection
options.body: Pause both warning PRs until maintainers choose a runtime/doctor mismatch detector instead of install-time messaging.

recommendation.title: Accept postinstall advisory after repair
recommendation.body: Keep this PR direction if it becomes profile-aware and includes real postinstall warning proof for a listening gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits at the gateway service/update boundary where steipete has recent service-name and maintainer history.
